title: Steel fish tape, 1/8 in x 50 ft

sources.citation: Steel fish tapes 1/8 in wide in a 50 ft length, wound in a case (two makers' product pages read 2026-11-15, makers not named in content: 1/8 x 0.045 in and 1/8 x 0.060 in tapes with a formed or double-loop end). 50 ft = 15 240 mm exactly (NIST SP 811): the longest conduit run it reaches.

game-design: the tape is taken to push round at most 360 degrees of bends (four 90-degree elbows) in one run, the same total a code-compliant EMT run may have between pull points (NFPA 70-2023 Art. 358.26, cited by number and paraphrased). A real tape's limit depends on bend radius, fill and lubricant; no published figure was read. P3 checks no conduit code rule; P4's inspector will.

game-design: a fish tape pulls conductors through conduit (step pull) with no conductor size limit: its end takes any building-wire size the conduit holds. Conduit fill is P4's inspector's; P3 stores what it needs and checks none of it (plan, P3 fence).
